messages:
maya: Heads-up — after the sidecar rollout on prod-edge we started seeing tenant invoice deltas for a small set of customers. ran a quick diff and the missing events line up with requests routed through the new telemetry sidecar.
liam: Oh interesting. Are the events not emitted, or are they emitted but missing tenant attribution?
anika: Looks like the sidecar is doing adaptive sampling and it rewrites some route headers when it forwards to the metering proxy. tenant_id header gets dropped for requests that hit the sampling path.
maya: Exact. Example from the logs: ```TRACE sidecar: forwarded req id=0x9f2a path=/v1/generate headers=(x-route=fast-sample) -> metering-proxy; tenant_id=null``` so the metering pipeline sees an untagged request and punts it to fallback-bucket which currently maps to anonymous usage (not billed correctly).
sam: That explains the negative invoice deltas we saw for those accounts. We have metric spikes on metering.events_unattributed and invoice.delta_alerts for a handful of tenants.
ops-ci: deploy-bot reports the sidecar rollout (ff:edge-metric-sampler=true) completed yesterday 03:12 UTC across us-east-1.
maya: Short-term hotfix brainstorm: 1) ensure sidecar preserves X-Tenant-ID header on forward; 2) add deterministic fingerprinting at proxy side that falls back to tenant header; 3) mark sampled events with a sampling-rate header so downstream can inflate counts.
liam: 1 is safest and smallest. If the sidecar accidentally strips headers due to header normalization layer in the envoy config, we can patch and rollback in 30m.
anika: Confirmed it's an envoy transform we enabled for header dedupe. Reverting that transform should restore tenant propagation. But we should also add observability: per-tenant sampling-rate and sampling-path label in the metering topic so invoice previews show sampling bias.
sam: For the longer term we should avoid using anonymous fallback bucket as a sink for untagged traffic. Maybe emit an explicit 'untagged' metric and surface it in invoice preview UI (console) with a link to rollout timeline so CS can proactively reach out.
maya: Agree. Also need to consider replay: can we reconstruct missing attribution by matching request ids in the profiling logs? We still have raw request traces in s3 for ~72h.
liam: We can correlate request-id -> session-id -> tenant in most cases. But some customers use ephemeral API keys so correlation will be partial. I can write a backfill job to rehydrate metering events for affected dates with a conservative matching window.
ops-ci: Note: backfill job will increase load on the ingest topic. Recommend running during low-traffic window and rate-limit writes to prevent downstream aggregation backpressure.
anika: UX/console ask: add a dashboard panel for 'sampling path attribution' with a breakdown by tenant id and sampling-rate. Also surface a red flag if invoice preview delta > 0.5% for last 24h.
sam: For rollout policy: disable ff:edge-metric-sampler for all tenants flagged with high-traffic until we have header-preservation tests in the e2e. Then re-enable only under canary with header-propagation verification.
maya: I'll open a quick PR to revert the envoy transform and add a unit test for header passthrough. Liam, can you own the backfill plan (script + throttle)?
liam: Yep. Will sketch a job: read traces (s3://redwood/edge/traces/2026-03-20/*), join on request-id, emit events to metering-write topic with header: {tenant_id, sampling_path, sampled=true}. Will cap at 50rps per partition.
anika: I'll file a console ticket to add the sampling panel and an incident note template for CS outreach.
ops-ci: deploy-bot: rollback patch for envoy-transform rolled out to 6 hosts in prod-us-east-1 at 03:48 UTC. Health checks green.
maya: Good. Post-mortem checklist: cause, immediate fix (revert transform), monitoring gaps (no sampling-rate metric), longer-term improvements (deterministic fingerprint, console UX, safe fallback bucket). Assign owners and ETA.
liam: I'll include estimated invoice impact numbers and run the backfill dry-run against staging to validate idempotency.
sam: One follow-up — add a release checklist item: "metering header propagation validated in canary" before any sampling or routing optimization is enabled.
maya: Agreed. Thx everyone. I'll ping ops on the rollback thread and post an incident note once we have backfill numbers.
